tells.1: Stock apology bookends ('please accept my apology,' 'sorry for any inconvenience') clash with the bolted-on 'just hit reply.'
tells.3: Even, impersonal polish: each sentence does one job and no particular person is speaking.
tells.4: Mechanically trimmed close — the bare 'reply to this message' drops the courtesy the rest of the note sets up.
tells.5: 'That's not the experience we want you to have,' sandwiched between a thank-you and a second apology.

reason: Version 2 sounds like one agent taking ownership — spoken rhythm, contractions, and a concrete offer to help — while 5 is corporate-empathy filler and 1 mixes stiff templates with a casual aside. I'd send 2 because it is clear and credible without the padding.
